title: Counter loop run to completion
statement: Let $M$ be a deterministic machine with $k$ Boolean work tapes and state $a$, and let $exit$ be an optional state. Let $w$ be a Boolean word with binary value $d$, and suppose the extra tape initially agrees with the word buffer at cells $cp+p$ for all integers $p$ with $-1\\le p\\le |w|$. Given an initial configuration $c$ and a run-length function $\\tau$, suppose that for every $r<d$, the $r$th round configuration is in state $a$, its run length is positive, every intermediate configuration at a positive time strictly before the round endpoint has a state different from $a$ and is not the designated exit, and the next round configuration is again in state $a$. If $T$ equals the sum of these round lengths plus $\\operatorname{overhead}(w,d+1)$, then the counter-loop machine reaches the done configuration at time $T$, with the extra tape filled with true symbols on cells $cp$ through $cp+|w|-1$. At all earlier times it is neither done nor escape; through time $T$ the extra head lies in $[cp-1,cp+|w|]$, and the first $k$ work-head positions at each time coincide with those in a run of $M$ from some round configuration $c_r$, at a time $u$ satisfying either $r<d$ and $u\\le\\tau(c_r)$ or $r=d$ and $u=0$.
hypotheses_covered: Machine $M$, state $a$, optional exit, and initial configuration $c$
Initial extra-tape buffer agreement for all $-1\\le p\\le |w|$
For every $r<d$, each round starts and ends in state $a$
Every strictly intermediate positive-time state avoids $a$ and the designated exit
The specified total time $T$ equals the round-length sum plus counter overhead
